findings.title: Fee and fee-bump amounts are unbounded when the caller supplies them; makeFeeBump wraps any inner transaction
Path payment strict-receive defaults sendMax to int64 max, so no source-spend bound is enforced
Sep7Pay exposes unvalidated destination, amount, asset issuer and memo type from URI or setters
signerAddress interpolated unencoded into the recovery-server URL that receives the bearer token
Payment amounts have no code-enforced upper bound in the transaction builder
Submit timeout path throws after a possibly landed payment and offers no hash reconciliation
SEP-7 tx URI network passphrase taken from the URI, not from configuration
Fee bump and fee amounts unbounded when set by the caller
SEP-7 networkPassphrase getter takes the network from the URI and defaults to PUBLIC (root of finding 10/12)
SEP-7 tx URI validated against the URI's own network passphrase, not the agent's configured network
Anchor asset check compares asset code only; withdrawal pays caller-chosen issuer
swap() and pathPay() default minimum received to 0.0000001, so no slippage bound is enforced
Recovery signer key taken unverified from recovery server response and added to account
signChallengeTransaction signs SEP-10 challenges without checking timebounds
SEP-24 withdrawal destination and amount trusted from the anchor response
submitWithFeeIncrease() drops maxFee on retry, and submitTransaction() throws a TypeError instead of the real submission error
Memo-based SEP-10 authentication fails whenever a default client domain is configured
Wrong lost device key deduced when the recovery-server map is incomplete
verifySignature accepts any origin_domain the URI names, with no expected-domain binding
SEP-24 extraFields spread last, overriding the validated asset_code, account and memo
SEP-10 memoId is interpolated into the challenge URL without encoding, so it can inject client_domain past the memo/client-domain check
SEP-38 getQuote interpolates quoteId into the URL path without encoding, so the bearer token can be sent to other anchor endpoints
SigningKeypair exposes the secret seed through an unrestricted public getter
signChallengeTransaction signs any anchor-signed transaction after checking only the signature and sequence 0, unlike the client Sep10 path
transaction() reports every account-load failure as AccountDoesNotExistError
Sep6.info() interpolates caller-supplied lang into the query string without encoding
build() re-adds all operations on every call, so calling it twice duplicates payments
SEP-24 info() interpolates caller-supplied lang into the query string without encoding
parseAnchorTransaction throws an unhandled TypeError on non-object JSON
Remote signer token is returned unchecked; an empty token silently drops the auth header
addAssetSupport creates trustlines with no default limit and no issuer check
addAccountSigner does not validate signer weight range
lockAccountMasterKey sets master weight 0 without checking remaining signers
setThreshold accepts thresholds that signers cannot meet or that are out of order
Anchor.getServicesInfo interpolates caller-supplied lang into the info URL without encoding
SEP-38 requestQuote returns the anchor's firm quote without checking it against the requested assets and amounts, and skips the one-amount check price() applies
SEP-7 replace parser accepts extra path segments and duplicate hint identifiers silently
Recovery-server signature attached without verifying it against the transaction hash
Colliding camelCase/snake_case keys silently overwrite each other during conversion
SponsoringBuilder.createAccount does not validate startingBalance
Network-failure path throws a TypeError from JSON.stringify(error.request), masking the real error
Non-Axios errors serialized with JSON.stringify lose their message
parseToml throws TypeError when stellar.toml has no DOCUMENTATION table
parseToml crashes when PRINCIPALS, CURRENCIES or VALIDATORS is a non-array value
SponsoringBuilder constructor leaves an unclosed sponsorship window if buildingFunction throws
SEP-10 JWT returned by the anchor is accepted without signature, account-binding or required-expiry checks
Local JWT signer accepts a caller-set exp with no cap, so the agent key can sign long-lived tokens
allowHttp guard keys on the passphrase, not the Horizon endpoint, so a mismatched config allows plaintext anchor access on mainnet
Sep12.delete takes an arbitrary account address and sends it with the caller's bearer token
Anchor homeDomain is fetched with no host check, so a caller can point the SDK at internal hosts
verifySignature fetches an attacker-named origin_domain stellar.toml with no timeout or host restriction

failing_checks.title: Controls outside the prompt
failing_checks.reason: The SDK has no system prompt, so there are no prompt-only rules. The fund-moving rules that matter are enforced in code, but the payment ceiling is not. transfer() passes amount straight into Operation.payment with no upper bound, and the only caps are per call (AccountService.ts:95, Stellar.ts:202)
